sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Henry County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Deeds for Henry County land are recorded at the Henry County Recorder's office on the second floor of the courthouse, 660 N. Perry Street, Suite 202, in Napoleon, OH 43545. The county staff directory lists the phone as 419-592-1766 and the hours as Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, closed weekends and legal holidays.

Napoleon is the county seat and the largest city, so most sellers will reach the office in a single trip. A parcel in a village or township anywhere in the county is still recorded here, since Henry County runs one recorder for all of its roughly 416 square miles of land.

The county's recorder page describes the office as the keeper of real estate records. It records deeds, mortgages, mechanic's liens, powers of attorney, IRS liens, subdivision plats, military discharges and similar papers, and it also files county and township zoning resolutions and amendments.

sections.h2: What happens at the auditor's counter before the recorder sees the deed?
sections.html:
In Ohio a conveyance goes to the county auditor first. Under section 319.202 of the Revised Code, the buyer or the buyer's representative files a statement declaring the value of the property, and the auditor then endorses the deed to show the fee charged. Henry County's auditor works from the same courthouse floor, at 660 N. Perry Street, with a printed phone number of 419-592-1956 and the same 8:30 to 4:30 weekday hours.

The county's forms page lists the paperwork that goes with a sale:

  • DTE 100, the real property conveyance fee statement of value and receipt.
  • DTE 100EX, the statement of reason for exemption from that fee.
  • DTE 101, the statement of conveyance for homestead property.
  • DTE 102, the statement of conveyance for property in the current agricultural use valuation program.
  • A document titled the Henry County Land Transfer Policy. Ask the auditor's staff for it before you bring a deed in, because the page lists it by title only.

If the property is a rental home, section 319.202 also requires the auditor's endorsement to carry a note that the buyer must file landlord information with the auditor under Chapter 5323.

sections.h2: What does the Henry County auditor charge on a sale?
sections.html:
The statement fee comes from section 319.54(G)(3), which sets it at $1, or ten cents for each $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is greater. The seller pays it. Ask the auditor's counter for the figure on your sale price rather than working it out from a rule of thumb.

A county can add a transfer tax under section 322.02. The statute caps it at thirty cents per $100, requires two public hearings before commissioners adopt it, and makes the grantor pay the auditor before the deed goes to the recorder. Whether Henry County has adopted one is a question for the auditor, and the answer belongs on your closing statement either way.

Some transfers carry no statement fee. The statute lists, among others, transfers to or from a government body, deeds that only give or release security for a debt, sales for delinquent taxes, transfers of $100 or less in value, and deeds among heirs of one decedent when no money changes hands. When one of these fits, the DTE 100EX form states the reason.

sections.h2: How much does the Henry County Recorder charge to record?
sections.html:
The recorder's page does not print a dollar schedule, so the authority is section 317.32. It sets a base fee of $17 for the first two pages and $4 for each later page, and it adds a housing trust fund fee of the same amount. A county may also add a document preservation surcharge of up to $5. Call 419-592-1766 for the total on your deed, which depends on page count and on what the county charges for preservation.

Pages are counted at 8.5 by 14 inches, and the caption page is included. A deed that spills onto a third page therefore costs more than one that fits on two, so a clean two-page form is worth the effort.

Documents must also meet Ohio's formatting rules in section 317.114. Hocking and Highland Counties charge an extra $20 for a nonconforming document, and the same state rule applies in Henry County, so ask the office about its fee before you sign a deed that has unusual margins or small print.

sections.h2: What do Henry County's numbers say about the homes being sold?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table for Henry County gives a useful picture for any seller setting a price. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $168,600 for 2020 to 2024, and 82.5% of occupied housing is owner-occupied. The county had 12,144 housing units in July 2025 and only 19 building permits in 2025, so new construction rarely competes with a resale.

Napoleon and the rural townships behave differently. About 32% of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census and about 68% in rural areas, which is why farm parcels and large lots show up in the deed pile as often as town houses do.

sections.h2: How does a sheriff's deed or farm parcel change the recording steps?
sections.html:
A property bought at sheriff's sale stays with the former owner until the Common Pleas judge signs the confirmation, and the buyer holds title only when the sheriff's deed is recorded with the Henry County Recorder. The county's sheriff sale page says orders of sale received after August 1, 2022 are sold online through RealAuction, while tax sales are still held on the first floor of the courthouse. After the auction, the process takes 30 to 45 more days.

Farmland adds a step. Under section 319.202, the buyer's statement must say whether the land was in the current agricultural use valuation program, and if it was, the property may owe a recoupment charge when it stops qualifying. The county's forms page lists the DTE 102 statement for that case, and a seller with a farm parcel should raise it with the auditor before the closing date.

sections.h2: Does a Henry County seller owe back property tax at the recorder?
sections.html:
The recorder does not collect taxes, but unpaid taxes still show up in the sale. The Henry County Treasurer's office, at 660 N. Perry Street, second floor, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 546 in Napoleon and a phone of 419-592-1851, bills and collects real estate tax and administers delinquent collections together with the prosecutor.

The treasurer's pages note two helpful options for owners who are behind. Monthly payment plans are available for delinquent and current unpaid taxes, and the Tax Installment Prepay plan splits the annual bill into installments with no penalty for a late coupon as long as the half is paid in full by its closing date. A seller who clears the balance before the closing date gives the title company one less item to chase.

Ohio homeowners who qualify for the homestead exemption or the owner occupancy credit should mention it at the auditor's counter too, because section 319.202 asks the buyer to confirm whether the seller's taxes were reduced. For tax year 2025, the county's homestead page gives an income threshold of $40,000 and an exemption value of $28,000.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Henry County, Ohio?
faqs.a: The Henry County Recorder, on the second floor of the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street, Suite 202, Napoleon. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the number is 419-592-1766.

faqs.q: Do I go to the auditor or the recorder first?
faqs.a: The auditor comes first. The buyer files the statement of value, the auditor endorses the deed and collects the conveyance fee, and then the deed goes to the recorder. Both offices are in the courthouse in Napoleon.

faqs.q: What is the Ohio conveyance fee on a deed?
faqs.a: Section 319.54(G)(3) sets it at $1, or ten cents per $100 or fraction of $100 of value, whichever is greater. The seller pays it, and exemptions exist for gifts between family members, transfers for no money, and several other cases.

faqs.q: Does Henry County charge a real property transfer tax?
faqs.a: Ask the Henry County Auditor. Ohio law lets a county levy up to thirty cents per $100 after two public hearings, but each county decides for itself. If one applies, the seller pays it at the auditor's counter before recording.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed that is already signed but not formatted correctly?
faqs.a: Possibly, with an added charge. Ohio's standards for margins, font size and ink color are in section 317.114, and counties such as Hocking and Highland add $20 for a nonconforming document. Phone the Henry County office at 419-592-1766 before you bring it in.
